where-to-start.label: I don't know where to start
hints: Start by identifying the GitHub API endpoint you'll need. The public user endpoint returns profile data — once you know what comes back, decide which pieces belong in your interface.
Sketch a simple layout on paper: an input at the top, profile info below, then repo stats. Build the input and fetch logic first — everything else follows from the API response.
Try fetching data for a known username like 'octocat' in your browser or a quick script. Seeing real JSON makes the rest of the build much clearer.

stuck-planning.label: I'm stuck planning
hints: Break the app into three screens in your head: input → loading → results. You only need to build one screen at a time.
List the five requirements as checkboxes. Pick the easiest one — usually the username input — and ship that before touching anything else.
Don't plan for edge cases yet. Get the happy path working with one username, then handle empty states and errors.

debugging.label: I'm debugging
hints: Open your browser's Network tab and check if the API request is going out. A 404 usually means the username is wrong; a CORS error means you need a server-side fetch or proxy.
Log the full API response to the console before trying to render it. Most bugs come from assuming field names that don't exist in the actual JSON.
If data shows in the console but not on screen, the issue is in your render logic — check that you're accessing nested properties correctly.

give-hint.label: Give me a hint
hints: The GitHub REST API endpoint for a user profile is GET /users/{username}. No auth needed for public profiles.
Repository languages live inside each repo object. You'll need to aggregate them across repos to find the most-used ones.
For a responsive layout, stack profile and stats vertically on mobile. A simple CSS grid or flex column works well at 390px width.
